lines: This test fails on the original code.
It passes with the fix.
An AI wrote that fix, for a real bug in Rich, a Python library with fifty seven thousand stars.
ThePolisher proved it works, in about three minutes, for about two cents.
AI can write a fix in seconds.
Then someone has to check it.
Does it fix the bug?
Did it break something else?
Are the tests real?
Is the pull request description true?
Maintainers are flooded with AI pull requests, and they can't tell which ones work without checking each one.
ThePolisher is a verifiable agent on Meta's Muse Spark. Its pull requests come with proof.
Paste an issue from a public Python repository.
Muse Spark reads the issue and the code, and writes three fixes at once.
Each one runs in its own Modal sandbox, and the tests pick the best one, not the model.
Then four agents work in parallel.
CodePolish owns the fix and its tests.
SecurityPolish reviews it, and a security scan must find nothing new.
DocPolish updates the docs.
WritePolish writes the pull request, and fills in the project's own template.
Every revision goes through a gate.
If it breaks something that used to pass, it is thrown out.
Muse Spark is multimodal, so it reads the screenshots in an issue too, and says what it saw.
At the end, the whole test suite runs on a fresh copy of the repo.
The proof card shows the new test failing on the original code because of the bug, then passing with the fix.
The first draft is kept, so you can see what the agents added.
Same issue, same model.
The numbers come from the sandbox, not from the model grading itself.
It was tested on seventeen real, open issues, in nine popular projects we don't control, with the list committed before any run.
ThePolisher proved fourteen fixes.
A single prompt with the same model proved seven.
All seventeen cost sixty six cents.
When it can't prove a fix, it says so.
Three issues have never been proven, and they are in the published results.
In the latest full run, the median was five and a half minutes.
Repository code only runs in sandboxes with no secrets.
Issue text is treated as untrusted data.
Agents learn from past runs, but only from runs the tests verified.
And nothing is pushed for you.
The pull request opens only when you click, and confirm.
Everything you saw was built during this hackathon, starting October twenty seventh.
AI writes fixes.
ThePolisher proves them.
